title: routing: feed GPU pool capacity signals into breaker + routing decisions
author: Ravi Menon
description:
Motivation: The routing service currently makes “best effort” decisions based on static pool configs + breaker state transitions driven primarily by request failures/latency. During overload we were late to react because we weren’t incorporating real-time GPU pool saturation/queue pressure, which contributes to tail latency collapse and cascading retries. This PR wires GPU pool capacity signals into the routing decision path and breaker inputs, and introduces an explicit “shed hint” path so downstream layers (gateway/runtime) can shed deterministically when we’re over target capacity.

What’s in this PR: (1) Introduces CapacitySignalsClient in routing-service that queries control-plane capacity summaries per (region, pool, model_class, tier) with bounded fanout + caching (stale-while-revalidate). (2) Adds capacity-derived inputs to breaker evaluation: pool_utilization, sched_queue_depth, inflight_requests, and soft_throttle (control-plane computed) with configurable staleness tolerance. (3) Updates routing selection to prefer pools that are below soft_throttle and to avoid pools that are “hard saturated” unless customer policy explicitly opts into degrade/fallback. (4) Adds ShedHint to RoutingDecision: NONE | EDGE_SHED_RECOMMENDED | RUNTIME_SHED_RECOMMENDED with an associated reason code (e.g., POOL_SATURATED, QUEUE_DEPTH_HIGH, SIGNAL_STALE). Routing returns the hint to callers; it is gated by the existing overload-protection feature flag and not exposed to customers directly yet. (5) Observability: metrics for signal freshness, capacity sampling latency, and decision outcomes. Adds tracing attributes for selected pool + capacity snapshot hash.

Behavioral notes: - We do not open the breaker purely on high utilization; we require either (a) sustained soft_throttle with queue depth above threshold or (b) hard_saturated from control plane. This reduces flapping and aligns with ADR-0148 hysteresis expectations. - If signals are stale > max_staleness_ms we fall back to current behavior (breaker-only) and emit routing_capacity_signal_stale_total. - Dedicated: capacity inputs are read but shed hints default to NONE (Dedicated customers shouldn’t see “unexpected” shed behavior from hosted heuristics). This is configurable and matches the Dedicated alignment plan.

Testing: unit tests for capacity snapshot merging + staleness logic; integration test using a fake capacity-service that simulates step-function load (queue depth spikes) and validates routing avoids saturated pools and emits EDGE_SHED_RECOMMENDED when no safe pool exists.

Rollout: behind feature flag routing.capacity_signals.enabled (default off). The plan is to enable in us-east canary pools for 1–2 hosted models (per ENG-4834) and validate error mix + latency before expanding.

Follow-ups: - Wire ShedHint through gateway admission control response mapping (separate PR / ENG-4822). - Tune thresholds per region/model_class once we have canary data (ENG-4828 / ENG-4840).

Refs: ENG-4825, ADR-0148, incident notes in INT-1190.
commits: routing: add CapacitySignalsClient and in-memory cache with SWR
routing: extend breaker inputs with capacity snapshot fields
routing: prefer under-throttle pools and avoid hard-saturated pools
obs: add metrics for signal freshness + decision outcomes; trace attrs
tests: fake capacity-service integration test for overload scenario
conversation: Mina Haddad (review): The overall direction looks right, but I’m worried about decision instability when signals jitter. Can you clarify which fields actually influence breaker open vs just pool preference? Also what’s the staleness policy during partial outages of the capacity service?

Ravi Menon (author): Good call. In this PR: pool selection uses soft_throttle + hard_saturated as preferences/avoidance; breaker open only happens when (soft_throttle && queue_depth_high) sustained for N windows OR hard_saturated. Added comments in BreakerEvaluator and a config knob for min_windows. For staleness: max_staleness_ms defaults to 1500ms; if exceeded we bypass capacity-derived inputs and emit stale metric. Partial outages: SWR cache continues serving last good snapshot until staleness threshold, then disables capacity inputs (falls back to current behavior).

Elena Popov (review): Please add explicit guardrails so we don’t accidentally route to a pool with SIGNAL_STALE and treat it as “healthy”. Maybe a metric label for stale vs fresh decisions? Also, do we need to cap cardinality on labels (pool/model/tier/region)?

Ravi Menon (author): Added routing_decision_capacity_freshness{fresh|stale} and removed pool_id from the metric label set (kept pool_class). Per Allison’s earlier review, we only label by region, tier, model_class, and decision_outcome. Pool_id is logged and added as a trace attr (sampling applies).

Peter Holtz (review): The integration test uses a 250ms poll interval and the default cache TTL at 300ms. In prod we’ve seen control plane lag up to ~1s under load. Can we make these parameters explicit in config and document safe defaults? Also what happens if the capacity service returns “unknown” for a pool?

Ravi Menon (author): Updated: poll_interval_ms, cache_ttl_ms, and max_staleness_ms are now explicit config with defaults (250/500/1500). Added docstring in flags.ts and a note in the PR description. For unknown pools, we mark snapshot as partial and do not emit hard_saturated/soft_throttle; routing treats it as neutral (no preference) and increments routing_capacity_unknown_pool_total.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics look mostly good now. One more: can we avoid emitting per-model-name labels? model_class only please. Also add a histogram for capacity fetch latency with coarse buckets.
Ravi Menon (author): Done. Removed model_name label entirely (only model_class). Added routing_capacity_fetch_latency_ms histogram with buckets [5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000].

Ethan Park (approve): Looks good. Thanks for the SWR fallback; that’s important for control plane resilience. Please make sure the control-plane proto change is backward-compatible (field numbers) — I checked, it is.
Mina Haddad (approve): Approved after the jitter/staleness clarifications + metric label fixes. Let’s keep an eye on canary decision stability once enabled.
release_notes: Internal: Routing service now consumes control-plane GPU pool capacity signals to influence breaker inputs and routing decisions (gated). Adds internal shed hints (not customer-facing yet) plus new metrics/tracing for capacity freshness and decision outcomes.
